what: Every verb the deploy gate runs, and all it runs (scripts/vps/gate/GateRules.ps1 reads this). A verb is one script of main, run on the box by the gate broker from a checkout of origin/main, with only the parameters named here. A parameter's rule is 'switch' (no value), 'text' (the text rule below) or a pattern its value must match whole. 'fixed' goes on every run of that verb; a fixed word with no hyphen is the value of the fixed parameter before it, so a verb can be held to one channel. 'build': true marks a live verb: its line must name main's full commit with -Build, and the broker runs it only when main is at exactly that commit (the build Patrick gave his word for); -Build never reaches the script. 'out' is the parameter that names the folder the verb writes its files into: the broker sets it to a folder of the run's own and sends back what lands there. 'afterDeploy' lists the environments a step after a deploy (deploy/after, #5186) may run the verb after: the deploy agent runs only those, held to this file as the signed Release carries it. Only a verb whose fixed words hold it to that environment, or one that only reads, goes on it; Check-ProdParity does not, since the agent runs it after every dev Deployment itself (#5180). 'reads' names the files and folders (a folder ends in /) of main that decide what the verb does on the box beyond its script, such as the keys Grant-BoxKey puts there: auto-merge holds a change to any of them for Patrick as it holds the script (scripts/ops/Auto-Merge.js, #5726). 'reads' names every file of code the verb's script runs as well, as scripts/ops/Verb-Files.js finds them: node scripts/ops/Verb-Files.js --write puts them in, and tests/test-6184-verb-files.js fails when a verb runs a file its reads does not name (#6184). 'onlyReads': true marks a verb that changes nothing on the box and only reads it: the broker's read lane runs it beside whatever else runs, from a checkout of its own, so a deploy or a content build never holds up a ping or a read (#6231); every other verb runs one at a time.
